predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The abstract states 'Memory Mosaics v2 matches transformers on the learning of training knowledge (first dimension) and dramatically outperforms transformers on all inference-time tasks (second and third dimensions), demonstrating universal superiority in zero-shot and few-shot scenarios.' However, Table 1 shows that on the zero-shot benchmarks (which are part of the first dimension, persistent-knowledge storage and retrieval), Memory Mosaics v2 and transformers perform essentially identically (both average 52.2 for large models). Claiming 'universal superiority in zero-shot' is inconsistent with the data.

The text says 'Memory mosaics v2 outperforms transformers on 4k task-length by 1.4%∼5.6%.' Table 3 shows transformer small 4k: 39.4, MMv2 small 4k: 45.0 (difference 5.6) and transformer large 4k: 57.7, MMv2 large 4k: 59.3 (difference 1.6). The correct range is 1.6% to 5.6%, not 1.4% to 5.6%.

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper cites 'Beck et al., 2025' in the main text (section 3.2: 'Inspired by recurrent-style networks [Peng et al., 2023; Gu and Dao, 2023; Beck et al., 2025]' and Appendix D: 'xLSTM [Beck et al., 2025]'). However, the reference list entry for that work shows the year as 2024 ('Maximilian Beck, et al. xLSTM: Extended Long Short-Term Memory. Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, 37:107547–107603, 2024.'). The in-text citation year does not match the publication year in the bibliography.

Equation (4) is derived from Equation (3) under the assumption that all key vectors have the same squared norm. From (3): f(k) = sum_i [ e^{-β ||k-k_i||^2} / sum_j e^{-β ||k-k_j||^2} ] v_i. If ||k||^2 = ||k_i||^2 = constant c, then ||k-k_i||^2 = 2c - 2k^⊤ k_i, so e^{-β ||k-k_i||^2} = e^{-2βc} e^{2β k^⊤ k_i}. The factor e^{-2βc} cancels in numerator and denominator, leaving e^{2β k^⊤ k_i}. Equation (4) shows e^{β k^⊤ k_i} instead of e^{2β k^⊤ k_i}; the factor of 2 is missing unless β is implicitly redefined.

The short-term memory is defined as storing key-value pairs from t−h+1 to t−1 (eq. 10). With h=256 (as stated in Section 4), the range from t−255 to t−1 contains 255 tokens, i.e., h−1 tokens. The paper repeatedly refers to the 'short-term memory window size h=256', implying h tokens are stored. This is a minor inconsistency in the window size definition.

The abstract states: 'A Memory Mosaics v2 trained on one trillion tokens achieves substantial improvements on these tasks, completely eliminating the need for additional training data that transformers require.' Section 6 shows that transformers trained on 8T tokens can match Memory Mosaics v2 on some tasks (e.g., semantic-label in-context learning), and still lag on others. The claim of 'completely eliminating the need' overstates the findings, as more data can partially close the gap.
